summary.name: Monny
summary.one_liner: Monny is a free, open-source native macOS menu bar app that monitors CPU, memory, disk, network, sensors and battery, and sets the built-in macOS charge limit.
use_cases: Monitor CPU, memory and network usage from the menu bar
Limit battery charging to 80% to preserve battery health
Find which process is using a specific port and quit it
Check remaining AI tool plan quota before a long task
Review system history and temperature sensors in a dashboard
summary.what_it_does: Monny runs in the macOS menu bar and reads CPU, memory, disk, network, temperature sensors and battery state, with a dashboard showing history from 1 minute to 7 days and top processes. Its process list can be searched by name, PID or port, and it flags processes above 80% of one core for a minute or more. For battery, it sets the charge limit built into macOS rather than running a helper, and it shows battery health, cycle count and power draw. It can also show optional AI tool plan usage limits using each tool's own sign-in on the Mac, and can send one-time notifications for events such as high heat or low battery.
notable: Open source under the MIT license, no account, analytics or telemetry
Charge limit uses the native macOS setting with no helper or root access
Process lookup by port number, with quit for a single process
Optional AI plan usage limits shown next to CPU and memory
caveats: Requires Apple silicon, macOS 15 or later; the charge limit needs macOS 26.4 or later and a Mac with a battery
Not yet notarized by Apple, so macOS may block the first launch and requires a manual allow step
Sensor availability differs between Mac models; unavailable sensors are shown as unavailable
